doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Peers versus critics
summary: Bryant says peer recognition outweighs critics; Liston says her friends, men and women, are what matter.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: You know what to me, Melba, is people worry about having critical acclaim and all that kind of stuff, but to have my peers recognize me means more to me. I don’t know about you, but it’s always meant more to me than the critics, because I know my peers understand more than the critics do.
I wanted to get your idea about that.
Because your peers are not going to leave you like critics will. They’ll praise you one day and the next day, if they’re not feeling too good, they’ll dump you or dump on you or whatever.
I don’t care about the – what do you call them? Peers or something. But my friends – all the guys are my friends. And the girls . . .
That’s what I mean. I call them my peers, because we’re doing it in the same business. We’re dedicated just like they are, even though we’re female.
